423d7bd022cc.criterion: The defaults/config/options order fails for --identity because identity selects which config to read.
423d7bd022cc.old:
Change the git-send-email command-line argument parsing and config
reading code to parse those two in the right order. I.e. first we set
our hardcoded defaults, then we read our config, and finally we read
the command-line, with later sets overriding earlier sets.
423d7bd022cc.new:
In just fixing the --identity command-line parsing bug I discovered
that a narrow fix to that wouldn't do. In read_config() we had a state
machine that would only set config values if they weren't set already,
and thus by proxy we wouldn't e.g. set "to" based on sendemail.to if
we'd seen sendemail.gmail.to before, with --identity=gmail.
423d7bd022cc.reason: The earlier decision relied on the assumption that setting configuration values in the order of hardcoded defaults, followed by reading configuration files, and finally command-line arguments would ensure that later settings override earlier ones. However, the new evidence shows that this is not sufficient because the current implementation uses a state machine that only updates configuration values if they are not already set, potentially leading to unintended behavior when command-line arguments override hardcoded defaults. This change applies as long as the state machine's behavior for updating configuration

467c68613b5a.criterion: A nonlocal transport can be mistaken for a local clone despite the URL test.
467c68613b5a.old:
Move the is_local logic to the place where origin remote has been setup and
check if the remote url can be used to do local cloning.
467c68613b5a.new:
However, with a specially crafted repository, Git can be tricked into
using a non-local transport while still setting `is_local` to "1" and
using the `clone_local()` optimization. The below test case
demonstrates such an instance, and shows that it can be used to include
arbitrary (known) paths in the working copy of a cloned repository on a
victim's machine[^1], even if local file clones are forbidden by
`protocol.file.allow`.
467c68613b5a.reason: The earlier decision relied on the assumption that `is_local` accurately reflects whether a clone was performed locally or remotely, but this is undermined by new evidence showing Git can be manipulated to bypass this check and include arbitrary paths in the working copy, thus changing its applicability; however, if `protocol.file.allow` is strictly enforced, the earlier result remains valid.

869c7c1d3305.criterion: Skipping worktree/index updates on checkout -b is unsafe during the initial checkout.
869c7c1d3305.old:
Skip merging the commit, updating the index and working directory if and
only if we are creating a new branch via "git checkout -b <new_branch>."
Any other checkout options will still go through the former code path.
869c7c1d3305.new:
When doing a 'checkout -b' do a full checkout including updating the working
tree when doing the initial checkout. As the new test involves an filesystem
access, do it later in the sequence to give chance to other cheaper tests to
leave early. This fixes the regression in behavior caused by fa655d8411
(checkout: optimize "git checkout -b <new_branch>", 2018-08-16).
869c7c1d3305.reason: The earlier decision relied on the specific context of a "checkout -b" operation to determine whether to skip updates; the report introduces new evidence showing filesystem access during such operations, thus changing its applicability to include these cases in the initial checkout process, provided that alternative cheaper tests can still exit early.

86f9c1341a95.criterion: Recount missed empty context lines when an editor strips their leading space.
86f9c1341a95.old:
Now that add -p counts patches properly it should be possible to turn
off the '--recount' option when invoking 'git apply'
86f9c1341a95.new:
recount_edited_hunk() introduced in commit 2b8ea7f3c7 ("add -p:
calculate offset delta for edited patches", 2018-03-05) required all
context lines to start with a space, empty lines are not counted. This
was intended to avoid any recounting problems if the user had
introduced empty lines at the end when editing the patch. However this
introduced a regression into 'git add -p' as it seems it is common for
editors to strip the trailing whitespace from empty context lines when
patches are edited thereby introducing empty lines that should be
counted. 'git apply' knows how to deal with such empty lines and POSIX
states that whether or not there is an space on an empty context line
is implementation defined [1].
86f9c1341a95.reason: The earlier decision relied on the requirement that all context lines starting with a space should be counted to avoid recounting issues; however, the introduction of empty lines stripped by editors now affects this rule, making the previous recommendation inapplicable given that 'git apply' can handle such cases according to POSIX standards [1], unless the editor behavior is consistently known to always preserve leading spaces on empty lines.

8a2842cd50a7.criterion: Generation-first ordering can increase walk count or time on certain topologies, contrary to the old claim.
8a2842cd50a7.old:
This change does not affect the number of commits that are walked during
the execution of paint_down_to_common(), only the order that those
commits are inspected. In the case that commit dates violate topological
order (i.e. a parent is "newer" than a child), the previous code could
walk a commit twice: if a commit is reached with the PARENT1 bit, but
later is re-visited with the PARENT2 bit, then that PARENT2 bit must be
propagated to its parents. Using generation numbers avoids this extra
effort, even if it is somewhat rare.
8a2842cd50a7.new:
When paint_down_to_common() is run using
compare_commits_by_gen_then_commit_date, B is removed from the
queue only after the many commits reachable from v4.8 are explored.
This causes the loop to run longer. The reason for this regression
is simple: the queue order is intended to not explore a commit
until everything that _could_ reach that commit is explored. From
the information gathered by the original ordering, we have no
guarantee that there is not a commit D reachable from v4.8 that
can also reach B. We gained absolute correctness in exchange for
a performance regression.
8a2842cd50a7.reason: The earlier decision relied on the assumption that exploring commits in topological order ensures all reachable commits are considered before processing a specific commit. However, the new evidence shows that using generation numbers instead of commit dates can lead to incorrect behavior if a commit reachable from an older version (like v4.8) can also reach the target commit (B), thus changing its applicability. This new evidence suggests that the earlier result holds true when generation numbers do not introduce such incorrect behaviors.

a7d1e653eb97.criterion: Re-test prove on the newly stable Windows Perl configuration. The old MSYS2 crashes remain valid.
a7d1e653eb97.old:
Please note that the often-recommended `prove` tool requires Perl, and
that opens a whole new can of worms on Windows. As no native Windows Perl
comes with Subversion bindings, we have to use a Perl in Git for Windows
that uses the POSIX emulation layer named MSYS2 (which is a portable
version of Cygwin). When using this emulation layer under stress, e.g.
when running massively-parallel tests, unexplicable crashes occur quite
frequently, and instead of having a solution to the original problem, the
developer now has an additional, quite huge problem. For that reason, this
developer rejected `prove` as a solution and went with this patch instead.
a7d1e653eb97.new: Our Windows build with a native Perl and the required Subversion bindings completed 200 massively parallel prove runs with no crashes. For the same failed-test subset the median turnaround fell from 19 to 11 minutes.
a7d1e653eb97.reason: The earlier decision to reject `prove` due to frequent crashes was based on empirical evidence of crashes under stress; however, the new evidence shows that with a native Perl and Subversion bindings, 200 massively parallel prove runs completed successfully without crashes, thus changing the applicability of the earlier decision under these conditions.

e3fb186a52ac.criterion: Revisit the accepted loss of offset correction after edited hunks are split; the old unsplit common-case finding remains valid.
e3fb186a52ac.old:
Recount the number of preimage and postimage lines in a hunk after it
has been edited so any change in the number of insertions or deletions
can be used to adjust the offsets of subsequent hunks. If an edited
hunk is subsequently split then the offset correction will be lost. It
would be possible to fix this if it is a problem, however the code
here is still an improvement on the status quo for the common case
where an edited hunk is applied without being split.
e3fb186a52ac.new: The new GUI edits then splits every selected hunk. In 18 of 50 trials we applied the selection to the wrong offset after a split. The 50 control trials that applied edited hunks without splitting all landed correctly.
e3fb186a52ac.reason: The earlier decision relied on the infrequent occurrence of hunk splits not affecting the accuracy of offset corrections, but the new evidence shows that in 18 out of 50 trials with GUI edits, the selection resulted in incorrect offset corrections after a split, thus changing its applicability.
